title: V Sge TESS eclipses agree with the accelerating Smak (2022) ephemeris in 2019-2022; the 2024 eclipses end 9 min early but start on time, so they do not show a faster period decrease
abstract: Question: Do the eclipse times of V Sge after 2020 follow the period-decrease fits of Smak (2022), a quadratic fit with constant dP/dt and a cubic fit with dP/dt that grows in size, and do they agree with the dP/dt that doubles in 89 yr that the merger prediction of Schaefer et al. (2020) implies? Method: We measured eclipse times in TESS 2-min data of 2019, 2022 and 2024 with six estimators and cycle bootstrap errors, and season times from SuperWASP and ASAS-SN. We compared them with the Smak predictions (his data end in 2020.6), with a 2.0-min season jitter from his published minima. We also timed the ingress and egress branches separately, and fitted local parabolas and a model in which dP/dt grows exponentially, anchored to the Smak values. Results: In 2022 the cubic fit predicts the eclipse to 1.0 min; the constant-dP/dt fit is 6.1 min late (2.2 sigma). In 2024 the eclipse centres are 10.8 +- 2.7 min before the cubic prediction in both sectors, and the 2024 low-state cycles are the most offset, so the 2024 outbursts do not cause the shift. But only the egress moved (9 min early); the ingress was on time or late, and the eclipse became 9-20 min narrower. This is a change of eclipse shape, not a clear orbital phase shift. With centre or egress times, a growing dP/dt (doubling in 50-65 yr) is preferred and constant dP/dt is disfavoured (Delta chi2 6-12). With ingress times, the local dP/dt is (-5.5 +- 1.2)e-10, as the cubic fit predicts, and constant dP/dt is allowed. The 89-yr doubling agrees with all three timing definitions (Delta chi2 at most 2.9). Limitations: Only one TESS season after 2022 exists; ASAS-SN errors are too large; pre-1998 minima enter only through the Smak fit results; the best orbital clock within the eclipse is not known without radial velocities.

display.caption: O-C of V Sge primary eclipses relative to the Smak (2022) cubic ephemeris. Grey: literature minima and season means (1998-2020). Blue: TESS eclipse centres; green: ingress-branch times; orange: egress-branch times. Dashed: Smak quadratic (constant dP/dt). The shaded region is after the Smak data. In 2024 the centres and egress are about 10 min early, but the ingress is not.

Left: mean TESS eclipse profiles in 2019, 2022 and 2024 on the Smak cubic ephemeris. Right: ingress and egress times (mean of 30/50/70 percent depth) relative to their 2019-2022 means. In 2024 only the egress is early, and the eclipse is narrower.

Delta chi2 profiles of the growth rate g of dP/dt (1/doubling time) for 1998-2024 eclipse times, with two anchors from Smak (2022). Blue: TESS centre times; orange: egress; green: ingress; dotted: centre times without 2024. Vertical lines: constant dP/dt and the 89-yr doubling of Schaefer et al.
